Paragraph:
Translation: My whole body is trembling, and my hair is standing on end. My bow Gandiva is slipping from my hand, and my skin is burning.

Purport: There are two kinds of trembling of the body, and two kinds of standings of the hair on end. Such phenomena occur either in great spiritual ecstasy or out of great fear under material conditions. There is no fear in transcendental realization. Arjuna's symptoms in this situation are out of material fear—namely, loss of life. This is evident from other symptoms also; he became so impatient that his famous bow Gandiva was slipping from his hands, and, because his heart was burning within him, he was feeling a burning sensation of the skin. All these are due to a material conception of life.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Arjuna's somatic symptoms peak into a full-blown panic attack, causing a complete loss of psychomotor control and intense sensory overload.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: He drops his legendary weapon (Gandiva) and experiences a burning sensation across his skin. The commentary clarifies that these intense physiological reactions are strictly rooted in 'material fear' (fear of death and loss), not spiritual realization.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna is now completely incapacitated, both psychologically and physically.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.somatic Symptoms: Piloerection (hair standing on end), Tactile hallucinations (burning skin), Psychomotor impairment

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Dehatma-buddhi (The bodily conception of life, which is the root cause of all material fear and anxiety)
Bhaya (Intense material fear that disrupts both the mind and the physical body)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: This verse demonstrates the paralyzing power of material consciousness. When an individual identifies completely with the temporary physical body and its relationships, the threat of death or loss induces absolute terror, stripping away one's strength, purpose, and spiritual equilibrium.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Arjuna is in the throes of a severe panic attack. The psychological distress has caused a complete collapse of his nervous system's regulation. The dropping of his bow signifies a loss of basic motor function and self-efficacy, while the 'burning skin' indicates severe sensory dysregulation and hypersensitivity brought on by acute trauma.
